state.assembly: The builder assembles original pinned vendor bytes, 20 checked allocated sections from 12 linked components, three explicit NOBITS zero fills, 61 fixed-site detours and one checked bridge word edit. DATA includes a fresh startup header and zero-filled plan/session/per-boot identity slots. Two independent builds yield identical raw CODE/DATA. Assembly/readback passes 15 test groups including malformed ELF, wrong sites/symbols, overlap, BSS corruption and provisioned loader storage rejection.
state.replay: Observer constructors initially load ELF metadata and fixture state. Before execution, all CODE (2 MiB) and SRAM (32 KiB) are overwritten with 0xcc, then only the produced raw CODE/DATA are copied. Section/hook readback and source hashes are checked. No ELF bytes are injected after these raw copies. The test separately publishes a synthetic plan/request address and fixed synthetic identity, models platform memory/MMIO/grants/IRQ scheduling, and explicitly sets a held direct callback lease after native parking. Full native startup/RX/TXDONE/BA bodies pass: 3072 shared packet claims, 1792 independent page claims, eight parked harts, six invalid-loader cases and eight TXDONE failure controls with retained resources.
state.provider: The current Linux 6.18.52 provider C is extracted, compiled and run with modeled firmware requests/resource lookup/mapping/memcpy_toio. All 273 loader matrix cases and seven cases using the actual raw pair pass ASan/UBSan/leak checks. Pair copies read back byte-identical; missing/empty/oversized/invalid-plan cases leave both destinations unchanged. Probe boot trigger and real per-boot publication are not exercised.
state.deployment: The production recipe still installs vendor CODE/DATA. The new raw pair is local and not packaged, flashed or physically accepted. Unprovisioned artifacts stop before native IRQ setup. Physical reservation/containment, real loader publication, strict host setup, remaining owners/hot lifecycle/postgate, drains/recovery and actual clients remain open.

claims.raw: Full native replay executes assembled raw CODE/DATA without post-load ELF byte injection, under explicit modeled platform/provider inputs.
claims.immutable: The stored raw DATA does not bake in the test boot identity, request address or held lease.
claims.physical: These passing tests prove safe physical replacement and complete NPU acceptance.
claims.copy: The actual current provider C passes exact-pair copy/failure tests with modeled external dependencies; this is not a physical loader or boot-trigger proof.

unbaked_identity.instructions: Do assembly and replay directly support claims.immutable? Treat runtime synthetic publication as different from stored artifact initialization.

criteria.supported: The claim follows for stored bytes, not runtime state.
criteria.contradicted: Fixture identity/request/lease is encoded in stored DATA.

criteria.supported: The stated scope is fully supported.
Physical replacement and all NPU acceptance are established.
